item.description: Apart from Copenhagen, Stockholm and Helsinki, no other major European city currently meets the revised EU limits for nitrogen dioxide and particulate matter - exposure to which caused a combined 216,000 excess deaths in 2023 alone.

item.title: [DW] British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
item.description: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.

item.title: [DW] UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
item.description: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.

item.title: [DW] Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
item.description: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.

item.title: [DW] EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks
item.description: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.

item.title: [DW] Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?
item.description: The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?

item.title: [DW] What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
item.description: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

item.title: [DW] Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul
item.description: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.

item.title: [DW] UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
item.description: A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.

item.title: [DW] Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy
item.description: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.

item.description: Rwanda is set to host a so-called EU return hub. No formal deal has been announced as technical details still need to be sorted out in negotiations. The hope is to start deporting people next year.

item.description: The EU agreed on Monday (16 November) to sanction 30 people and two organisations over Russian cyberattacks and disinformation campaigns targeting Europe, as researchers uncovered thousands of fake accounts used to target election campaigns.

item.title: [EU Observer] What Marine Le Pen and Alice Weidel are planning for Brussels
item.description: The AfD's Alice Weidel envisages reducing EU powers under existing rules within three years, pursuing treaty reform within seven, and using Germany's budgetary leverage along the way. Hot on her heels, Marine Le Pen is looking towards national elections across Europe to build a coalition of like-minded governments.

item.description: MEPs are debating their position on the issue this week

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Prague doesn’t want Nazis’: Activists block Slovak far-right MEP from conference about deporting immigrants
item.description: In a heavily guarded Prague hotel, anti-migrant ideologues from Germany, Hungary and Czech Republic rallied together in support of a petition to deport foreigners that was rejected by the EU on rights grounds. MEP Milan Mazurek, previously convicted of inciting hatred towards Roma, was stopped from going inside by antifascist protesters.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU Commission clears UniCredit’s Commerzbank takeover, tells Berlin not to stand in the way
item.description: The European Commission has waved through Europe’s biggest cross-border bank takeover since the financial crisis, and warned it would “react accordingly” to any national government trying to block it.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ghost of Yalta returns, amid fears that Trump, Xi, and Putin will carve up Ukraine and Europe
item.description: History’s warning from Yalta hangs over today’s secretive talks, as European leaders answer an existential carve‑up threat with a clumsy committee instead of a single hard‑nosed envoy who knows the Kremlin’s playbook.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Is Europe ready to defend itself against cyberattacks?
item.description: Bomb threats, election interference, espionage, and sabotage. Cyberattacks are becoming an increasingly serious threat across Europe, affecting everything from public services to critical infrastructure. So, how prepared is Europe to deal with them?

item.title: [EU Observer] THIS WEEK: EU piles on more Russia sanctions, a crunch UK-EU summit, and budget wrangles
item.description: The draft new sanctions list includes Russia's richest woman, Tatyana Kim, as well as dozens of Russian banks and propagandists, with both France and Germany saying that the extra sanctions were already a done deal.

item.title: [DW] The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture
item.description: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

item.title: [DW] Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
item.description: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.
